solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Southern tip to northern tip, this island will get cooler

indicators.note: in a down entry the southern tip is the bottom letter and the northern tip the top, so the last letter of the island's name goes up to the front

parts.note: an esky is the Australian word for a portable cool box

explanation.surface: A tourist promises that a Scottish island will feel chillier from one end to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: move the island's last letter, E, to the top and the island becomes ESKY, an Australian cool box.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the large Inner Hebridean island off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Cosmetics supplement

definitions.meaning: face paint, powder and lipstick taken together
to top up or complete a shortfall, as in topping up the difference

explanation.surface: A short label for a beauty product added to a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a collective word for face paint; the two-word verb means to complete an amount that falls short.

clue.text: Look down, but don't push someone over cliff

parts.note: the opposite of pushing is pulling
a person, any one, gives the article A
something that runs over its time runs long
the sheer side of a cliff is its face, as a climber says

explanation.surface: A warning on a clifftop: peer down if you like, but don't shove anyone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look down' reads as an instruction to peer over the edge; it is the definition, meaning look glum.
explanation.definitionFit: To look down is to appear dejected, and this idiom means wearing a miserable, gloomy expression.

clue.text: Error reports doubly detailed

indicators.note: doubly says the shortened piece is written out twice in a row
read as de-tailed: the word for reports loses its last letter

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, a boom

explanation.surface: A newspaper's mistake is described twice over in great detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'in detail' but means de-tailed: BOOM loses its M, and 'doubly' gives BOO twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A booboo is an informal word for a silly blunder or slip.

clue.text: Support given by everyone to both halves of afternoon game

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece written beneath another holds it up, so the word for everyone goes under each half of the afternoon abbreviation

parts.note: PM, post meridiem, marks the afternoon
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everyone backs both teams in an afternoon match.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry a piece written under another supports it, so 'Support given by everyone to both halves' puts the word for everyone beneath each letter of the afternoon abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall-mall was an old mallet-and-ball game, a forerunner of croquet, which gave its name to the London street.

clue.text: Bizarre tale about nutty nudist impersonating a tortoise

indicators.note: about means the first rearranged piece goes around the second
bizarre says the letters of tale come out in a strange new order
nutty, meaning crazy, says the letters of nudist are scrambled

explanation.surface: An odd story about a mad naturist who pretends to be a tortoise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bizarre' gives TEAL and 'nutty' gives STUDIN; 'about' splits the first round the second. The surface suggests a story about a nudist, but both words are only letter supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Testudinal is the adjective from Latin testudo, a tortoise, meaning shaped or shelled like one.

clue.text: Sharp piece by The Scotsman when reporting Alpine ceilidh?

indicators.note: reporting means spoken out, so we hear a phrase rather than see it

parts.note: a party in the Alps could be a ski and do, a do being a party, and a ceilidh is a Scottish dance party

explanation.surface: A Scottish newspaper writes up a knife at a mountain dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Scotsman' looks like the Edinburgh newspaper but simply means a Scot. A ceilidh is a Gaelic social gathering with music and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A skean-dhu is the small dagger tucked into a Highlander's stocking as part of formal kilt dress.

clue.text: Stopped The Guardian of Wordplay heading north?

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means reading upwards, so the pieces run backwards
of joins the guardian to the wordplay, which comes first in the reversed string

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
ward in its old sense is guard or watch, as in watch and ward

explanation.surface: A newspaper's puzzle editor halts the crossword setter's progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Guardian' looks like the newspaper. The pieces PUN and WARD, read upwards, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that has drawn up has pulled in and come to a halt.

clue.text: Sanctioned Arthurian knight to open Book of Words

indicators.note: the knight goes into the dictionary's abbreviation, opening it up

parts.note: OED, the Oxford English Dictionary
Sir Kay was King Arthur's foster brother and seneschal

explanation.surface: A Round Table knight is allowed to launch a new dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to give it official approval, so sanctioned is an exact synonym.

clue.text: First book live backing groups …

parts.note: Gen, short for Genesis, the first book of the Bible

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for live is read backwards

parts.note: to live is to be: we are

explanation.surface: A debut book is supporting a live music act's bands.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology genera are the classification groups between family and species.

clue.text: … the people's holding account 25 per cent outstanding — it's not being settled

indicators.note: holding means the people's word wraps round the shortened account

parts.note: the laity are the ordinary lay people of a church; the 's makes the next word theirs

indicators.note: outstanding here means missing, standing out of the word for account

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed
a quarter of a four-letter word is one letter, the last L

explanation.surface: A congregation keeps a bill partly unpaid, which is why it is not settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like an unpaid debt but means missing: one of BILL's four letters goes. 'it's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lability is the quality of being unstable or liable to change, the condition of something never staying put.

clue.text: Doing employee's job, as mad ogre is seen to be?

definitions.meaning: the proverb says there is no point paying for help and then doing the work oneself

definitions.text: as mad ogre is seen to be
definitions.meaning: the words mad ogre hold a dog inside them, and mad means barking, so the ogre is both keeper and barker

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer explains why a raving monster behaves like a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: In MAD OGRE the letters A DOG sit inside, and 'mad' is barking, so the ogre fits both halves of the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb mocks anyone who hires help yet still does that work personally, as if the owner of a guard dog barked.

clue.text: More than one bookplate collector is touring house no end

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for is surrounds the shortened house

parts.note: to be is to exist: he exists

indicators.note: no end means the house loses its final letter

parts.note: Libra is one of the twelve astrological houses

explanation.surface: A sightseer is going round a house with no end of rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' stands for EXISTS, which wraps LIBR, Libra (a zodiac house) without its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex libris, Latin for from the books of, is printed on bookplates, and its collectors are named after the phrase.

clue.text: See 3
See red ale mixed with spirits …

definitions.meaning: to lose one's temper suddenly, to go mad
a hot drink of beer and spirits, often sweetened and with egg

explanation.surface: Seeing red ale laced with spirits, as a drinker might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See red' reads as a colour to look at, but it means fly into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang verb means to lose control in anger; the noun is an old mixed drink of beer, spirit and sugar.

clue.text: One stowing away aboard ship's left undying city

parts.note: on board a ship, port is the left-hand side facing forward

indicators.note: stowing away means the word for one is tucked inside the word for undying

parts.note: sad in its old sense meant firm or constant, steadfast
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A stowaway has been left alive in a city after a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: SAD here is the archaic sense, steadfast or constant, close to undying.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Said is the Egyptian city at the Mediterranean end of the Suez Canal.

clue.text: … so highly acidic call …

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the reading for a very strong acid on the acidity scale
to ring someone up on the telephone

explanation.surface: A sour remark is followed by a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PH ONE: a liquid with pH 1 is very strongly acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone up on the telephone is to call them.

clue.text: Urgent news stops departure

indicators.note: stops as in stops up or plugs: the word for news fills the departure

parts.note: an exit is a way out or a going
gen is slang for information or news

explanation.surface: Pressing news halts a departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or demanding immediate attention.

clue.text: … to cover the inside track

definitions.meaning: to put a layer on the inner surface, as of a coat or drawer

explanation.surface: Fitting a cover on the inside lane of a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to coat an inner surface with fabric or paper; the noun can be a rail route or track.

clue.text: See 12
Would that old bats fly in circles!

indicators.note: circles means the jumbled letters wrap round the letter for old
bats means crazy, so fly and in are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wistful wish that elderly bats would fly in rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the flying mammals but means mad, giving the jumble IFNLY; 'circles' then wraps that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a wish for something that is not so, as in 'were it only true'.

clue.text: If you're up, what you'll be in society's bad

definitions.text: If you're up, what you'll be in

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for society
addle as an adjective means rotten, as in an addle egg

explanation.surface: A slightly scornful remark about high society being in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means mounted on horseback, where a rider sits in this seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who is up on a horse sits in the leather seat strapped to its back.

clue.text: Sources of wood, good sort initially …

parts.note: fir trees supply timber
toff, slang for a gentleman, also a decent chap

explanation.surface: A timber merchant describes how a decent chap first sourced wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at the very start, before anything else, just like the adverb.

clue.text: See 3
… until penny drops close

indicators.note: drops means the letter for penny is let fall from the word

parts.note: pending means awaiting or until, as in pending further notice

explanation.surface: Someone waits for the moment of understanding, then the scene closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penny drops' is the idiom for finally understanding, but here P simply drops out of PENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: A close is a conclusion, the finish or end of something, like a story's last chapter.

clue.text: Dramatic goings-on in Tokyo inspiring trailblazer in sushi cuisine

indicators.note: inspiring in the breathing-in sense: the drama takes the letter into itself

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama

indicators.note: the trailblazer is the first letter, leading the way

explanation.surface: A Japanese stage show prompts a pioneer of sushi cookery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' looks like 'motivating' but means breathing in: NOH takes in S, the first letter of 'sushi'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food or grub, the stuff any cuisine serves up.

clue.text: When I choose a woven fabric

parts.note: twill is a fabric woven in diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: A shopper says they will pick a woven cloth whenever they like.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means whenever one wishes, as one pleases.

clue.text: Refined sharp piece about Government

indicators.note: about means the sword word goes round the letter for government

parts.note: a cutlass is a short curved sword

explanation.surface: A cultured blade is all about the Government.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-glass accent is a very posh, polished upper-class way of speaking.
